summary: Thomas Henry Thornton was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Merchant Taylors' School and St John's College, Oxford (~1851-1855), he became a Fellow at St John's College (1855), University of Calcutta (1875), and Vice-President of the University of the Punjab (1879).

Thomas Holbein Hendley worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St Bartholomew's Hospital (~1865-1869), joined the Indian Medical Service in 1869, and served as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta from 1898 to 1903.

Thomas Howley specialized in Indology and linguistics after attending Bishop Cowie's Grammar School. He served as Head-Master at Anglo-Vernacular School, became Professor of Tamil, Telugu and Hindustani at King's College London in 1861, and taught Telugu at Oxford (1878-1885).

Thomas Hudson-Williams was a linguist who studied at Ysgol Friars, Bangor University, the University of London, and Greifswald under Heinrich Zimmer. He spent his career at Bangor University, serving as Assistant Lecturer from 1896 and Professor of Greek (1904-1940).

Thomas James Mazanec works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Calvin University, CU Boulder, and Princeton University under Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser. He served as Assistant and Associate Professor at UC Santa Barbara.

Thomas Jülch specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, the University of Hull, Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich (PhD ~2005-2011). He was a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University from 2013 to 2019.

Thomas Kintaert is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. His career includes posts at the University of Vienna, where he was attested in 2009 and served as a Lecturer attested between 2022 and 2026.
Thomas Lumisden Strange was an Indologist. He received his education at Westminster School and the East India Company College between 1824 and 1826.
Thomas M. Hunter is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Dean at the University of Virginia and held an affiliation with the University of British Columbia attested in 2011.
Thomas Manning worked in Tibetology and Sinology. He was educated at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, from ~1790 to 1795 and later studied at Westminster Hospital between ~1801 and 1803.

Thomas Maurice worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oxford at both St John's College and University College (1774-1778, M.A. ~1774-1808) and served as Assistant-Keeper of Manuscripts at the British Museum from 1798 to 1824.

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong attested in 2018.

Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. He studied under Paul Thieme and Albrecht Wezler, served as an instructor at the University of Zurich in 1990, and became Arbeitsstellenleiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thomas Oldham was a geologist educated at Trinity College Dublin and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Director of the Geological Survey of Ireland (1846) and Superintendent of the Geological Survey of India (1851-1876).

Thomas Procter was an Indologist who studied at Jesus College, Oxford (1818-1824). He later held posts as a Fellow at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1824-1826) and as an Examiner at Fort William College in 1828.

Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and held posts at the University of Michigan, where he served as co-director attested in 1980 and was attested in 1991.
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy (~1782-1783) and Jesus College, Cambridge (~1784-1788).

Thomas Robinson was a scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1808-1816), where he earned his B.A., M.A., and D.D. He later served as the Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from 1837 to 1854.

Thomas Roebuck was an Indologist and linguist educated at the Royal High School. He served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St. George in 1811 and examiner at Fort William College from ~1811 to 1819.

Thomas Sebeok was a linguist who studied at the University of Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield and at Princeton under Roman Jakobson. He spent his academic career at Indiana University Bloomington from 1943 to 1991, becoming Distinguished Professor Emeritus.
